title: Lina and the Flying Scores
markdown:
The Sunny Meadow Summer Games were quite the grand event. Every year, when the sun warmed the meadows just so, making the buttercups glow like a carpet of tiny golden coins, all the creatures would gather for a day of friendly fun. And who was always there, nestled by the finish line with a neat stack of colourful cards and a very important quill? Why, that was Lina the otter. Lina loved things to be perfectly tidy. She had a special little booth made of smooth river stones and soft green moss, a cosy nook where everything was organised with the neatness only an otter, with her sleek fur and clever paws, could manage. Her favourite quill, tipped with a feather from a particularly chatty jay, waited patiently.

This year, the most exciting event, the one that always made the younger creatures wiggle with anticipation, was the Comic Relay. It wasn't about being the fastest, oh no. The fastest runner might win a pat on the back, but the funniest runner won the hearts of the meadow. It was all about being the most entertaining, the most delightfully silly. As the whistle blew, a clear, sharp note that cut through the hum of busy bees, the first runner, Barnaby Bear, lumbered off. Barnaby wasn't just running; he was doing a little jig, a happy wobble, and a grand, sweeping wave to the crowd that made everyone giggle until their tummies ached. Lina, with a gentle puff of air, carefully marked down on her first colourful card: ‘+1 for Jig, +1 for Wiggle, +1 for Wave.’ She held her quill with a steady paw.

Next up was Flora Fox, sleek and speedy as a dart. But Flora, you see, never just ran. She believed a run needed flair. She’d pirouette at the halfway mark, a graceful twirl that made her red fur swirl, then leap over an imaginary puddle with a flourish and a flick of her magnificent, bushy tail. Lina’s quill was busy, scratching away: ‘+1 for Pirouette, +1 for Leap, +1 for Tail Flick.’ She liked to think of these as bonus points for bravery and beauty.

Ah, but here's the thing. All these little flourishes, these delightful extra bits the animals added to their runs, they didn’t actually slow anyone down. Not one bit. They just made the race a lot more fun to watch. The spectators, from the tiniest field mice to the tallest storks, roared with laughter and cheered with delight. And Lina, bless her diligent heart, was trying her very best to score every single one. Her pile of cards was growing, each one a different hue of the rainbow.

Then came Bert the goat. Bert wasn’t known for his quiet grace. When Bert ran, he bounced. He didn’t just run; he bounded, he pranced, his hooves making little clippity-clop sounds on the grass. And every so often, when he felt particularly joyful, he let out a tremendously happy, "Baaa-ha-ha!" that sounded like a giggle mixed with a happy sneeze. Lina’s brow furrowed. She chewed on the end of her quill for a moment, a habit she had when things got complicated. ‘+1 for Bounce, +1 for Prance, +1 for …’ she squinted at her card, ‘…joyful Baaa-ha-ha.’ It was getting a bit much, even for Lina. Her neat little stack of scorecards, once a tidy tower, was now leaning precariously, threatening to spill its colourful secrets.

And what do you suppose happened next? As Bert the goat finished his spectacular, bouncing, prancing, baa-ha-haing run, a most peculiar thing occurred. A sudden, playful gust of wind, smelling faintly of dandelion seeds and the promise of summer rain, swept through the meadow. It wasn’t a grumpy, blustering wind, but a light, mischievous one that ruffled the tall grasses and made the little bluebells nod their heads. Whoooosh! It caught Lina’s prize-winning scorecards. Her careful tallies, her neat little marks, her colourful cards – they all lifted into the air like a flock of startled butterflies, scattering in every direction.

Lina gasped. Her whiskers quivered, trembling like tiny antennae. Her heart thumped like a rabbit’s foot. Oh dear! All her hard work, gone in a blink! She watched, with wide, worried eyes, as the cards tumbled and danced, a riot of colour against the brilliant blue sky. A yellow card, with Barnaby’s jig marks, fluttered near the tallest oak. A pink one, with Flora’s pirouette, spiralled towards the berry bushes. The air filled with the rustle of paper and the gentle sigh of the wind.

But here's the curious thing about the Sunny Meadow. When something unexpected happens, the creatures don't always frown. Often, they find a way to laugh. Coach Pippin, the wise old owl, who had been watching from his perch on the highest oak, hooted softly, a sound like a gentle chuckle. "Now this is the part I love to tell," he whispered to himself, his eyes twinkling like fallen stars.

The runners, who had just finished, didn't sigh or complain about the lost scores. Barnaby Bear, instead of trying to catch his own cards, used his big, gentle paws to nudge some colourful ones that landed near him towards Lina’s booth. Flora Fox, with a graceful sweep of her tail, gathered a few that landed near her, her movements as elegant as always. And Bert the goat? Well, Bert did what Bert did best. He bounced and leaped, not to win anything this time, but to playfully bat at the tumbling cards, sending them in gentle arcs back towards Lina’s booth. The other animals, seeing the fun, joined in, chasing the airborne colours, their laughter echoing through the meadow, a symphony of pure joy.

Lina, at first, tried to catch them, her little otter paws darting out. But soon, she realised something wonderful was happening. The wind wasn't destroying her scores; it was sharing them. Each card that fluttered down, no matter what colour it was or what marks it bore, landed near a happy face. The bright yellow cards, dotted with Bert's enthusiastic paw prints and maybe a smudge of grass, landed near the giggling younger rabbits. The soft blue ones, bearing Flora's elegant scribbles and a faint scent of wildflowers, drifted to the more thoughtful badgers.

When the last card finally settled, there were no neat piles, no precise scores. But there were smiles. Lots and lots of smiles. Bert the goat nudged a bright orange card towards Lina. "That one," he bleated, his voice warm and happy, "that one was for my extra-special landing!" Lina looked at the card, smudged with a bit of grass and a bright, cheerful paw print. It wasn't perfect, not by Lina's old standards, but it was… joyful.

Coach Pippin glided down from his tree, landing softly beside Lina. "Ah, Lina," he said, his voice as warm and comforting as the meadow sun. He gestured with a wing towards the happy scene. "Sometimes, the most important scores are the ones you can't count. The smiles, the laughter, the shared fun – those are the real prizes."

Lina looked around at her friends, her paws sticky with flower petals from helping gather the cards. The air was still filled with the happy hum of the games, the excited chatter of the younger creatures. She picked up a slightly crumpled green card, a little damp from the dew. It wasn’t a score anymore, not really. It was a memory of a playful wind, a bouncing goat, and a meadow full of pure, unadulterated joy. And that, my dear child, was a tally worth more than any number you could ever write down.
characters: Lina the otter, Bert the goat, Coach Pippin
